implementation.title: Safe-area-aware landscape two-column layout; portrait and desktop adapt without a title ScrollView. Existing saves require new-game confirmation.
implementation.exploration: Fixed aim slot plus interaction only when a target is available.
implementation.aiming: Fixed fire and lower-weapon slots; gun ammo doubles as manual reload. Beer and rocket do not show reload.
implementation.equipment: Direct selection of owned weapons and beer, with current counts. Pauses play and cancels input; resumes exploration with the touch sneak toggle restored.
implementation.healing: Shortcut beside HP only while injured and holding a usable herb. Inventory is accessible from pause.
implementation.input: A press belongs to the action present at pointer down. Mode/weapon changes, drag, cancel and disposal invalidate it. Removed stick/look surfaces cannot replay old pointer input.

coverage: Mac Control and secondary mouse compatibility

nativeChecks.title: All actions visible in landscape and portrait. New-game confirmation canceled, then existing game continued successfully.
nativeChecks.equipment: Owned handgun/shotgun and beer selectable; no shot or beer consumed by selection.
nativeChecks.systemBack: Flutter back-route dispatch on the iOS simulator closed the equipment overlay, restored playing and preserved sneak. Not an Android hardware-button test.
nativeChecks.stealthInteraction: The context appears as a noninteractive label with a single 72px destroy button. A native tap defeated one enemy, with zero shots.
nativeChecks.harnessNote: Two taps sent before the next widget frame reported missing targets. Re-queried live elements and completed the checks. Final reload reported no runtime errors.
nativeChecks.fixture: mobileControls disables enemies and seeds items for stable UI verification; it does not validate difficulty or campaign traversal.

limitations: Physical iOS/Android touch feel and long-session performance have not been tested in this change.
Mac release uses the same responsive UI; simulator screenshots do not establish physical-device performance.
